article_title: These Hong Kong bookshops let Chinese readers question their country - now the doors are closing

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly examining?
options: How pressure under Hong Kong's national-security and sedition laws is closing independent bookshops that offered space for critical ideas
Why Hong Kong readers have suddenly stopped buying all printed books
How mainland China is funding new independent bookshops in Hong Kong
Why high rent is the sole cause of every bookshop closure
tasks.correct_answer: How pressure under Hong Kong's national-security and sedition laws is closing independent bookshops that offered space for critical ideas
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה בוחנת כיצד חקיקה ואכיפה בתחום הביטחון הלאומי וההסתה מצמצמות חנויות עצמאיות ששימשו מרחב לרעיונות ביקורתיים.

tasks.prompt: What happened after police raided Greenfield Book Store and Have a Nice Stay?
options: Both shops were given government expansion grants
The shops began selling only imported textbooks
Five people were arrested on suspicion of displaying or selling items with seditious intent
All seized books were immediately returned without investigation
tasks.correct_answer: Five people were arrested on suspicion of displaying or selling items with seditious intent
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בפשיטות על שתי החנויות נעצרו חמישה אנשים בחשד להצגה או מכירה של פריטים בעלי כוונת הסתה.

tasks.prompt: How long had Greenfield Book Store been part of Hong Kong's independent bookshop scene?
options: About five years
Since the 2019 protests only
More than a century
About 50 years
tasks.explanation_hebrew: Greenfield נפתחה ב־1976 והודיעה על סגירה לאחר כחמישים שנות פעילות.

tasks.prompt: What does “the elusive red line” suggest in the bookshops' context?
options: The boundary of prohibited material is unclear and difficult to predict
A railway line does not reach the shops
Every forbidden title has a visible red cover
The shops know exactly which books are officially banned
tasks.correct_answer: The boundary of prohibited material is unclear and difficult to predict
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מתאר גבול משפטי או פוליטי חמקמק: בעלי החנויות אינם יודעים בבירור איזה חומר ייחשב אסור.

tasks.prompt: Why were independent shops especially important to some readers?
options: They sold only government-approved schoolbooks
They provided access to political, historical and cultural ideas that mainstream outlets might avoid
They allowed customers to publish newspapers without names
They were the only buildings allowed to host public elections
tasks.correct_answer: They provided access to political, historical and cultural ideas that mainstream outlets might avoid
tasks.explanation_hebrew: החנויות העצמאיות אפשרו לקוראים לפגוש ספרים ורעיונות ביקורתיים שלא תמיד הופיעו ברשתות המרכזיות.

tasks.prompt: Why can raids and arrests cause censorship beyond the shops directly targeted?
options: Other booksellers may remove sensitive titles because they fear uncertain legal repercussions
Every reader automatically receives a prison sentence
Police physically confiscate every book printed overseas
The law requires all shops to close after 50 years
tasks.correct_answer: Other booksellers may remove sensitive titles because they fear uncertain legal repercussions
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כאשר הגבולות אינם ברורים והמחיר המשפטי גבוה, גם חנויות שלא נבדקו עלולות לצנזר את עצמן מחשש להשלכות.

tasks.prompt: Give two examples of pressure on Hong Kong's independent book sector described in the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שתי דוגמאות קונקרטיות לאכיפה, סגירה או הגבלה המתוארות בכתבה.
expected_points: Police raided independent bookshops
Five people were arrested at Greenfield and Have a Nice Stay
Books or publications were seized as allegedly seditious
Greenfield announced closure after 50 years
Have a Nice Stay closed earlier than planned
Other booksellers or activists had been jailed, investigated or forced into exile

tasks.prompt: Why does the absence of a clear public list of forbidden books not necessarily protect booksellers?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר כיצד עמימות משפטית עלולה דווקא להגדיל פחד וצנזורה עצמית.
expected_points: Booksellers cannot reliably know which titles cross the legal line
Sedition or national-security concepts can be interpreted broadly
A later raid or prosecution can occur despite earlier assumptions
The risk encourages shops to avoid contested or sensitive material
Uncertainty can close civic space without a formal blanket ban

tasks.prompt: Summarise how Hong Kong's political changes have affected independent bookshops and their readers.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לתאר את תפקיד החנויות בעבר, את השינוי המשפטי־פוליטי ואת תוצאתו לקוראים ולחברה.
expected_points: Independent shops offered access to sensitive or forbidden-in-mainland-China ideas
Hong Kong once had a stronger reputation for open publishing and discussion
National-security and sedition enforcement intensified after the 2019 protests
Raids, arrests, seizures and closures have affected multiple shops
Booksellers face an unclear legal boundary and may self-censor
Readers lose spaces for questioning history, politics and national identity

tasks.prompt: Evaluate the claim that an independent bookshop can be part of civil society, not merely a retail business. Use evidence from the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג טענה מנומקת, להשתמש בלפחות שתי ראיות מן הכתבה ולהכיר גם בתפקיד המסחרי של החנות.
expected_points: Bookshops create physical spaces for discussion and community
They preserve access to diverse political, historical and cultural viewpoints
Readers can encounter ideas absent from mainstream outlets
Closures reduce opportunities for public questioning and solidarity
The shops still face ordinary business pressures such as rent and profitability
Raids and vague legal risks show that authorities may view their social role as politically significant
